quests.question: If the weather ___ good tomorrow, we will go to the beach.
quests.hint: In a real conditional (if + present), the subject 'the weather' is singular.
quests.explanation: In real conditional sentences, the verb in the 'if' clause follows standard agreement rules. 'The weather' is singular, so 'is' is correct.

quests.question: If the results ___ positive, the project will continue.
quests.hint: In the 'if' clause, 'the results' is plural - verb agrees with it.
quests.explanation: In conditional sentences, subject-verb agreement still applies normally. 'The results' is plural, so 'are positive' is correct.

quests.question: Not only the manager but also the staff ___ invited to the event.
quests.hint: With 'not only…but also', the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it ('staff' is plural).
quests.explanation: With 'not only…but also', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'The staff' is plural, so 'are invited' is correct.

quests.question: Not only the staff but also the manager ___ invited to the event.
quests.hint: With 'not only…but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('manager' is singular).
quests.explanation: With 'not only…but also', the verb agrees with the nearest subject. 'The manager' is singular, so 'is invited' is correct - even though 'the staff' is also mentioned.

quests.question: Not only the students but also the teacher ___ surprised.
quests.hint: The nearer subject is 'the teacher' (singular) - verb agrees with it.
quests.explanation: With 'not only…but also', the verb agrees with the nearest subject. 'The teacher' is singular, so 'was surprised' is correct.

quests.question: Not only the teacher but also the students ___ surprised.
quests.hint: The nearer subject is 'the students' (plural) - verb agrees with it.
quests.explanation: With 'not only…but also', the verb agrees with the nearest subject. 'The students' is plural, so 'were surprised' is correct.

quests.question: The government ___ introduced new spending cuts.
quests.hint: In standard English, collective nouns like 'government' take a singular verb.
quests.explanation: In standard English, 'government' is a collective noun that takes a singular verb when acting as a unit. 'The government has introduced' - not 'have introduced'.

quests.question: The government ___ divided on the issue of immigration.
quests.hint: When a collective noun's members act as individuals, British English often uses a plural verb.
quests.explanation: In British English, collective nouns like 'government' and 'team' can take a plural verb when the members act as individuals, not as a unit. 'The government are divided' is natural in British English.

quests.question: The band ___ recording a new album in Los Angeles.
quests.hint: The band acting as a single unit takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: When a band acts together as a unit (recording together), a singular verb is standard. 'The band is recording a new album'.

quests.question: The budget that was set at the beginning of the year ___ now been exceeded.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the budget' (singular) - the relative clause is descriptive.
quests.explanation: The subject is 'the budget'. The relative clause 'that was set at the beginning of the year' describes it but doesn't change the agreement. 'The budget has now been exceeded'.

quests.question: Two of the three patients who ___ treated have made a full recovery.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'who' refers to 'patients' (plural).
quests.explanation: Inside the relative clause 'who were treated', 'who' refers to 'patients', which is plural. The verb inside the clause is 'were'.

quests.question: The product that ___ launched last month has exceeded sales targets.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'that' refers to 'the product' (singular).
quests.explanation: 'That' refers to 'the product', which is singular. The verb inside the relative clause is 'was': 'that was launched last month'.

quests.question: The new policies, which ___ designed to reduce costs, have had unintended effects.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'the new policies' (plural).
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to 'the new policies', which is plural. The verb inside the relative clause is 'were': 'which were designed'.

quests.question: The report, which ___ submitted last week, highlighted several risks.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'the report' (singular).
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to 'the report', which is singular. The verb inside the relative clause is 'was': 'which was submitted last week'.

quests.question: A total of fifty volunteers ___ needed for the study.
quests.hint: 'A total of' with a plural noun takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'A total of fifty volunteers' takes a plural verb because the noun 'volunteers' is plural. 'A total of fifty volunteers are needed'.

quests.question: The total number of volunteers ___ fifty.
quests.hint: 'The total number of' is always singular - it refers to one figure.
quests.explanation: 'The total number of' is always singular, like 'the number of'. 'The total number is fifty' - not 'are fifty'.

quests.question: The survey results, together with the analysis, ___ submitted.
quests.hint: The main subject is 'the survey results' (plural) - 'together with' is parenthetical.
quests.explanation: 'Together with the analysis' is parenthetical. The real subject is 'the survey results', which is plural. 'The survey results were submitted'.

quests.question: Neither the price nor the quality ___ good enough.
quests.hint: 'Neither…nor' with two singular subjects takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: When 'neither…nor' joins two singular subjects ('the price' and 'the quality'), the verb is singular: 'neither is good enough'.

quests.question: Either the heating or the windows ___ causing the heat loss.
quests.hint: With 'either…or', verb agrees with the nearer subject ('windows' is plural).
quests.explanation: With 'either…or', the verb agrees with the nearest subject. 'The windows' is plural, so 'are causing' is correct.

quests.question: Either the windows or the heating ___ causing the heat loss.
quests.hint: With 'either…or', verb agrees with the nearer subject ('heating' is singular).
quests.explanation: With 'either…or', the verb agrees with the nearest subject. 'The heating' is singular, so 'is causing' is correct.

quests.question: The increase in global temperatures ___ alarming scientists worldwide.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the increase' (singular) - not 'global temperatures'.
quests.explanation: 'The increase' is the subject; 'in global temperatures' is a prepositional phrase. Since 'increase' is singular, 'is alarming' is correct.

quests.question: The effects of climate change ___ becoming more visible every year.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the effects' (plural) - not 'climate change'.
quests.explanation: 'The effects' is the subject; 'of climate change' is a prepositional phrase. Since 'effects' is plural, 'are becoming' is correct.

quests.question: The ability to manage stress ___ crucial in high-pressure roles.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the ability' (singular) - the infinitive phrase is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The ability' is the singular subject; 'to manage stress' explains what kind of ability. 'The ability is crucial' - singular verb.

quests.question: The skills needed to succeed in this industry ___ constantly evolving.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the skills' (plural) - the past participle phrase is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The skills' is the subject; 'needed to succeed in this industry' describes which skills. Since 'skills' is plural, 'are constantly evolving' is correct.

quests.question: A range of approaches ___ used to tackle this problem.
quests.hint: 'A range of' with a singular concept takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'A range of approaches' takes a singular verb because 'a range' is singular - we are talking about one range. 'A range has been used'.

quests.question: A variety of methods ___ tried before this one was selected.
quests.hint: 'A variety of' with a plural countable noun takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'A variety of methods' takes a plural verb because 'methods' is plural and each is distinct. 'A variety of methods were tried'.

quests.question: A series of meetings ___ scheduled for next week.
quests.hint: 'A series of' takes a singular verb - the series is treated as a single sequence.
quests.explanation: 'A series of' is typically treated as singular. 'A series of meetings is scheduled' - the series itself is one thing.

quests.question: The number of people living alone ___ increased dramatically.
quests.hint: 'The number of' is singular - it refers to one total count.
quests.explanation: 'The number of' is always singular. 'The number of people has increased dramatically' - not 'have increased'.

quests.question: A large number of elderly people ___ living alone.
quests.hint: 'A large number of' means 'many' - plural verb with a plural noun.
quests.explanation: 'A large number of' is similar to 'a number of' - it means 'many' and takes a plural verb. 'A large number of elderly people are living alone'.

quests.question: The proportion of women in senior roles ___ risen significantly.
quests.hint: 'The proportion' is singular - 'of women' is a prepositional modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The proportion' is the singular subject; 'of women in senior roles' is a modifier. 'The proportion has risen' - singular verb.
